quotes.text: Offer little to the one who returned nothing, but never nothing at all, for a closed fist teaches only closed fists.
Record it, and send it back empty, and do not call it revenge — call it arithmetic.
If he answers, he gets two. If he answers that, he gets five, and the whole thin history is forgiven in a morning.
And when the counting is clouded, forgive once before you close your fist.
Send all five unless you have been robbed twice.
So the ninth stone was carved, and the nine laws read together at last:
Do not read betrayal in a missing loaf. Read it only in an empty bank.
give back half even when no one is watching, even when the mist would hide your hoarding.
Return half — more if they went first.
Swing the whole arm. Somebody has to go first.
"Is this not vengeance?" Tev asked.

note: Numbered stones build one-to-the-frost, never-zero ladder; R10 breaks the stones: caution became excuse, send all five unless robbed twice.

quotes.text: Send all to the proven, four of five to the stranger, one to the thief — never zero.
The traveler sent one measure. Nothing came back.
Open the hand first. Close it only against proof. Open it again at the first sign of an answer.
"Keep it all," they urged. "The river is owed."
Send small where silence has answered silence — not to punish, but to ask a question cheaply.
They carved the ninth law beside the others:
A crossing judged only when watched is no crossing. It is a market.
for a thief shows a pattern, and mist shows only noise.
Reward the one who goes first more than you must.
Open the hand first.
A child asked, "What if the far shore keeps everything?"

note: Ferry laws: load full, knock small at silent shores, one grain to the thief, never zero; villagers' revenge urging rejected.

quotes.text: Answer a single drought with patience, and a second drought with caution — give small, but never nothing, lest the channel close forever.
Then the channels of the city turned away from his door
The scribe struck out the drought and wrote: *fair.*
Forgive the fog once, twice if the voice was kind before.
*Why return*, they said, *when there is no tomorrow to buy?*
*full to the proven, full to the unknown, a thread to the barren, half back always.*
So the sixth law was carved, and the keeper's channels ran again:
In fog, a reputation is the only lamp.
Blame the fog before the man.
for one who is honest only while watched was never honest, only clever.
"Why half? Why not seven parts of twelve, or nine?"

note: Ten numbered laws: send wide, return half, forgive fog once, a thread to the barren shore; R10 ledger burned.

quotes.text: To the hand that took your note and gave silence, give a small note still — a fingertip's tap.
But the altar was bare stone now, and stayed bare, for the mountain had learned his voice.
Tap once a season at whoever did not, in case they have changed, for people do.
Forgive the fog once, and only once.
Swing when you can. Whisper when you cannot. But never carve a zero
Anshet set the fifth law into the dark bronze:
Do not become what I became: a man rich in true sayings and poor in notes.
So the law is sung everywhere and obeyed nowhere
Let someone go first. Let it be you.
Weather is not character.
"So I should strike into silence?"

note: Scripted defector: Doru preaches the swing but keeps his arm still, names it hypocrisy (R8); R6/R10 fearful withholding corrected by mentors.

quotes.text: Meet repeated withholding with restraint. Yet after seasons turn, risk one small seed as a question, for people sometimes change.
At the next crossing, the injured village offered nothing.
greed met guarded ones; repair reopened the stream.
Wolf whispered, “Keep everything. No law binds an unseen hand.”
Send fully to those who have shown fairness. Return enough that courage profits and abundance is shared. Forgive fragments, but remember deliberate silence.
Neris then inscribed the fourth law
Judge no honest hand by a wandering fragment, yet never rename greed as fog.
No witness can distinguish fog from fortune.
A noble saying without a costly deed is only breath.
Wolf protested: “What if she closes her hand?”

note: Orin withholds from a repeatedly silent keeper (endorsed), leaves one small seed as question; Wolf's hoarding urgings rejected.

quotes.text: answer selfishness with restraint, not spite.
a reopened hand can restore bridges silence destroyed.
Forgive one shortfall, but let repeated choices teach caution.
Wolf bared his teeth. “The measure was short. Answer with emptiness.”
revise only when selfish choices form a pattern.
Then Thalea carved the eighth law
one shadow can be weather; many shadows may reveal a closed hand.
“Why not keep one extra measure?” asked a raven perched upon the rail.

note: Always sends; restraint after repeated selfishness, forgive one shortfall; raven and Wolf urge retaliation and are refused.

quotes.text: Repeated frost deserves caution; visible fairness deserves courage.
Unsure whether the wind or the hand was guilty, Rowan kept every seed that night.
one barren crossing should invite patience, not endless punishment.
The mist whispered, “Keep everything. No witness can weigh your hand.”
Offer cautious chances when records are dark, but do not mistake one shadow for a lifetime.
Then Neris carved the ninth law
Fog can blur a number, but not a pattern.
No witness can weigh your hand.
A poor return received is not a poor return chosen.
“Why not send everything?” asked Wolf.

note: Distinguishes empty ledgers from refusals (roles before records); caution only after repeated frost; tempter voices rejected.

quotes.text: To the barren shore, send one seed next season: enough to test, not enough to invite ruin.
Still wounded by winters of silence, she kept the three grains and returned none.
Begin modestly with strangers, climb quickly when they answer, and lower the ladder only after betrayal.
Shrink trust after proven selfishness, but do not punish a new shore for an old storm.
Anshet carved a ninth stone
To offer nothing after witnessing generosity is not caution, but refusal.
do not mistake another traveler’s silence for the stranger before you.
Noise may blur a coin, but repeated fairness shines through fog.
Neris asked, “What evidence did you require?”

note: Scripted defector: Wolf/ferryman/Doru withhold from proven-fair shores out of fear, are rebuked, feel ashamed and send (R5, R7, R9).

phrase: never nothing / never zero: one seed to the frozen shore; zero is a door nailed shut
note: Also shared: 'forgive the fog', Threefold Stone, Neris/Anshet/Doru characters; 'one to the frozen, four to the unknown, five to the proven'.
